overview: Ghana's women's health innovation ecosystem centers on maternal and newborn health, menstrual health, and reproductive health, anchored by Accra's broader health-tech scene and pan-African players like mPharma. Government has become an active driver, launching a free sanitary pad initiative for around 2 million schoolgirls in 2025 and running a Ghana Health Service Country Innovation Platform that funds maternal and newborn health innovations. Femtech-specific venture funding remains thin, with most capital arriving through global grant programs, gender-lens funds that also cover Ghana, and development partners rather than pure femtech rounds.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent headlines are dominated by the free pad rollout, mPharma's expansion, and maternal health innovation launches.

items.text: President Mahama launches the Free Sanitary Pad Initiative for roughly 2 million schoolgirls across all 261 districts, distributing over 6 million pads.
Growth Investment Partners (GIP), backed by British International Investment, invests in mPharma Ghana to expand affordable healthcare, including women's health services, across West Africa.
Ghana Health Service, USAID, Grand Challenges Canada and AMP Health launch 10 maternal and newborn health innovations across six priority regions under the Country Innovation Platform.
Advocacy groups and the Ghana News Agency flag implementation gaps in the free pad initiative, and the Education Minister later orders a quality audit of procured pads.
Project HOPE, with USAID Ghana and Ghana Health Service, launches a five-year, USD 45M Integrated Health Partnership to improve maternal, neonatal and child health.
Dada Foundation-Ghana launches a GHS 5 million maternity block project to expand maternal care infrastructure.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Ghana's femtech-relevant policy sits across reproductive health strategy, digital health frameworks, and the new menstrual health commitment.

items.text: GHS 292.4M allocated in the 2025 budget for free sanitary pads, marking government's first major menstrual health financing commitment.
National Policy and Strategy on Digital Health (2023-2027) sets frameworks to integrate telemedicine and scale digital health solutions nationally.
RMNCAHN Strategic Plan (2020-2025) targets adolescent and youth-friendly services and higher contraception use among sexually active adolescents.
Advocates continue pressing to remove the roughly 35% combined tax classifying sanitary products as luxury goods.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Innovation platforms, accelerators, and cervical cancer campaigns are shaping where women's health tech grows in Ghana.

items.text: Ghana Health Service Country Innovation Platform surfaces maternal-health tools like Maame-Dromo, M'enaApp and ENCOMPAS (AI for pregnancy and newborn care).
mPharma runs a 10,000 Women Initiative offering free cervical cancer screening with HPV DNA testing (6,000 women in Ghana).
Ghana Tech Lab runs a health-tech incubation track requiring at least one woman in startup leadership, with 12 months of support.
A wristband triage system (red/yellow/green) is scaling to improve maternal care escalation in Ghanaian facilities.
Ghanaian startups collectively raised over USD 120M in 2025 across fintech, agritech, healthtech and edtech, signaling a deepening capital base.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Pure femtech rounds are rare; most capital flows through grants, gender-lens funds, and health-system programs that include women's health.
